item.title: GAC acquires 50 per cent of FAW Toyota
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The Guangzhou Automobile Group (GAC) will take over the 50 percent stake in FAW Toyota currently held by FAW. The deal, which leaked about two weeks ago, has now been confirmed by all parties. Importantly, FAW Toyota is to continue operating as an independent company—for the time being, at least.

item.title: Redwood to repurpose end-of-life batteries from Rivian vehicles
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Rivian and Redwood Materials are expanding their existing partnership. In addition to providing stationary battery storage, Redwood will play a larger role in the future on behalf of Rivian in recycling production waste and reusing decommissioned EV batteries.

item.title: Wallbox installs 120 EV chargers at Montréal airport
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: In partnership with the Canadian electrical solutions provider EDP électrique, charging hardware firm Wallbox has installed 120 new EV charging points at Montréal Metropolitan Airport’s YHU terminal. An additional 48 chargers will be installed once construction of a new airport building is concluded, bringing the total up to 168.

item.title: Spectacular Prototype: Tesla Roadster Set for 2028 Release
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Tesla has put on a big show for the presentation of its new Roadster. However, little remains of the first prototype that Tesla unveiled back in 2017 - neither in terms of design nor technology. Although detailed technical information is still scarce. The presentation focused more on the features realised through a collaboration with SpaceX. However, this has little to do with a road-legal car in Germany.

item.title: New entry-level Cupra Tavascan launched in the UK
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Cupra has expanded its UK Tavascan line-up with the entry-level 'Origin' trim, a smaller 58 kWh battery option, and additional technology features. Prices now start at £39,995, while selected existing versions have also become cheaper.

item.title: Plug-in hybrids emit six times more CO2 than officially stated
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: The gap between official and real CO₂ emissions from plug-in hybrids continues to grow. According to a new analysis by Transport & Environment, PHEVs emitted on average about six times more CO₂ under real-world conditions in 2024 than official figures suggest.

item.title: Astra Electric: Opel introduces new base version for €36,490
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Opel is reducing the base list prices for its Astra lineup - by introducing the new 'Astra Start' equipment variant. As a result, the entry price for the Astra Electric has dropped by €1,900 - to €36,490. Customers will, however, have to do without features such as a heat pump.

item.title: Fastned increases charging revenue and accelerates network expansion
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Fastned significantly increased its charging revenue in the third quarter of 2026 during a period of rapid expansion. The fast-charging provider commissioned 17 new stations, secured 26 additional locations, and currently has 65 stations under construction.

item.title: Great Han: BYD launches 5.26-metre battery-electric saloon
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: BYD is launching its new electric flagship sedan, the Da Han EV - a.k.a the Great Han - in China. For years, BYD has positioned the sedan as a premium model alongside the E-SUV BYD Tang, which was also rebranded as the "Great Tang" this summer.

item.title: 20 electric trucks from Germany for Belgian logistics firm H.Essers
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The logistics company H.Essers, based in Genk, Belgium, is expanding its electric fleet with 20 new electric trucks. MAN and Mercedes-Benz Trucks have each delivered ten units. They will now be primarily deployed from the company's Belgian locations.

item.title: VW prepares battery recall for multiple ID. models in Europe
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Volkswagen is preparing a recall of several electric series in Germany and other European markets due to potential defects in high-voltage battery cells. As a precaution, they recommend that affected vehicles should only be charged up to 80 per cent.

item.title: Tesla’s plans for Grünheide expansion take shape
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Plans for the expansion of Tesla's German Gigafactory in Grünheide are becoming clearer. According to media reports, the US electric car manufacturer intends to significantly expand the site over the coming years - with a new, much larger production hall and additional infrastructure.

item.title: France and Germany propose 90 per cent CO₂ cut for new cars by 2035
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Germany and France are set to propose that carmakers cut fleet CO₂ emissions by 90 per cent by 2035, rather than the currently planned 100 per cent - with no requirement to offset remaining emissions. That's according to excerpts from a preliminary agreement paper which also point to stricter "Made in Europe" requirements as the two countries seek to reshape the EU's 'Auto Package'.

item.title: Green SM deploys its first electric taxis in the U.S.
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: A little over a month after entering Europe, Vietnamese electric ride-hailing service provider Green SM has expanded into North America, beginning with the US. This is the VinFast affiliate's ninth market globally.

item.title: Porsche Cayenne S Coupé Electric test: The PPE has moved a step further
item.dc:creator: Daniel Bönnighausen
item.description: 390 kW at the fast charger, 16 minutes from ten to 80 per cent, and a chassis that confidently and surprisingly calmly handles over two and a half tons around corners: The Porsche Cayenne S Coupé Electric promises fast stages and short breaks. In the test, it becomes clear how far Porsche has developed the PPE for this purpose – and why the noise level deserves closer attention during charging.

item.title: Citroën reimagines the 2CV Fourgonnette as a BEV
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: At the 2026 Paris Motor Show, Citroën is unveiling the 2CV Fourgonnette Concept, an electric reinterpretation of its iconic "boxy duck." The study builds on the equally new 2CV Concept, transferring its idea of a simple, lightweight, and relatively affordable electric car to a compact utility vehicle. However, there are no concrete plans for production as of yet.

item.title: Japan: Suzuki prices e Sky below BYD & Honda’s electric kei cars
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Suzuki has announced the starting price of the e Sky in Japan. The brand's first electric kei car will start at 2.12 million yen (~€12,000 euros), undercutting rivals from BYD and Honda. Sales are set to commence on 16 November.

item.title: Q-Park expands collaboration with software provider Greenflux
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Parking operator Q-Park is expanding its collaboration with Greenflux at its locations in Germany and Ireland. Previously, 1,700 charging stations at Q-Park sites in the Netherlands were successfully migrated to Greenflux's software system. This means Q-Park will now independently operate its parking garage charging stations at additional locations and no longer rely on third-party providers for controlling and billing charging processes.

item.title: DHL Freight deploys SuperPanther eTopas 600 in daily operations
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: DHL Freight has moved the first SuperPanther eTopas 600 produced in Europe out of testing and into regular commercial operation. The battery-electric heavy-duty truck has been operating out of the Netherlands and traveling to Belgium since September, covering approx. 2,000 km per week.

item.title: Tesla expands Supercharger network along South Korean highways
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Tesla is expanding its Supercharger network in South Korea. As part of a program by the Korea Expressway Corporation, new fast-charging locations will be built at 21 highway rest areas.

item.title: ‘Major’ OEM to test Gelion’s NES cathode platform
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Gelion has signed an agreement with an unnamed major automaker to test its sulphur-based 'Nano Encapsulated Sulfur' cathode technology. The OEM will evaluate the material in cells with liquid and solid electrolytes, as well as with lithium-metal and graphite anodes.

item.title: Changan and CATL to expand battery capacity to 75 GWh
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Changan and CATL want to significantly deepen their collaboration. In addition to expanding their joint battery cell capacity to 75 GWh, the partners also plan closer cooperation on solid-state and sodium-ion batteries.

item.title: Paris Motor Show: A revolving door of Chinese brands
item.dc:creator: Robin Engelhardt
item.description: For almost all Chinese automakers looking to break into Europe, attending a major motor show is a must. Some arrive quickly and leave just as fast, while others take their time but make a big impact. We took a look around Paris – and encountered brands ranging from familiar to completely unknown.

item.title: BMW launches sixth-gen battery production in Shenyang
item.dc:creator: Kasimir Hupe
item.description: The BMW Group has begun series production of its Gen6 high-voltage batteries for the Neue Klasse in Shenyang. Following Debrecen and Irlbach-Straßkirchen, the site in northeastern China is the third plant in the company's new battery network. In future, the energy storage systems produced there will power the Neue Klasse models that BMW will manufacture in China for the local market.

item.title: SuperPanther: eTopas 600 at centre of European growth strategy
item.dc:creator: Peter Schwierz
item.description: SuperPanther aims to rapidly scale up sales of its eTOPAS 600 in Europe. At the IAA Transportation, Frank Schulz, Head of European Sales, spoke with electrive about the first customer deployments, consumption figures, dual-CCS as a bridge to MCS, and the planned ramp-up to several hundred vehicles. His assessment of economic viability is particularly bold: he states that the electric truck is already more cost-effective than a diesel in terms of total cost of ownership (TCO).

item.title: Leapmotor takes over Thai business as it plots local assembly
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Signalling a stronger commitment to Thailand, Leapmotor has taken direct control of its local operations. It has also started evaluating plans for setting up local assembly.

item.title: Chinese government cuts state subsidies for EV manufacturers
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: China is cutting export tax rebates for vehicles with alternative powertrains. With exports being a key growth driver, this puts Chinese automakers under pressure - just as domestic sales are slumping.

item.title: Share charging to cut costs, Fraunhofer tells electric truck fleets
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Sharing charging infrastructure between companies could improve the economics of electric truck fleets, according to a three-year research project led by Fraunhofer IFAM. The study found that selling charging electricity to third parties can reduce fleet operating costs, while warning that grid connection capacity remains a key obstacle to expanding infrastructure at logistics hubs and industrial sites.

item.title: Europe is back: How VW, Stellantis and Co. shine in Paris
item.dc:creator: Robin Engelhardt
item.description: The Paris Motor Show is a magnet for the global automotive industry this week. Europe’s sector is making it clear at the industry event that it will not cede the electric vehicle field to China without a fight. Above all, Stellantis and VW are presenting numerous innovations. Here’s our live trade fair report from Paris.

item.title: Aito plans European expansion for autumn 2027
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The Chinese Seres brand Aito outlines its launch plans for Europe at the Paris Motor Show: In autumn 2027, the EV manufacturer intends to enter the European market. In Paris, the luxury automaker is already presenting the quartet Aito 9, Aito 8, Aito 7, and Aito 6.
